evidence.summaryExcerpt: The search turned up good evidence that Greek marble sculpture was painted, though nothing specific about eyes or lips. Clothing patterns: Paint traces showing embroidered patterns survive on the peplos of an Archaic kore from about 530 BC in the Acropolis Museum. The Phrasikleia Kore is a Parian marble statue that features prominent polychromy as seen in the hair and the dress.

evidence.summaryExcerpt: Brinkmann's reconstruction draws on visible remaining pigment and technical tools such as ultraviolet-visible absorption spectrometry and X-ray fluorescence to detect colour, engravings and painted patterns. Breadth of practice: A study of The Met's Cycladic collection in the 1990s found that nearly every example has traces of pigment.

claimResults.note: Standard claim; the summary describes pigment traces detected with UV and X-ray fluorescence.

evidence.restatement: Many Greek marble statues and reliefs were painted in colour; polychromy is well documented from pigment traces.
